issues.finding: Positioning/movement is safety-sensitive under the editorial charter. The public imperative setup and positioning language, together with Try this together/Try it together, function as companion-issued care instructions. A reference at the end or a private evidence caveat does not make this a descriptive summary of the authors’ view.
issues.suggestedRevision: Recast the public entry as a book perspective, with an opening and topic summary that explicitly describe the authors’ approach. Remove the imperative care checklist and use an appropriate Read more CTA/kind presentation. A reviewable opening direction is: The authors describe observing the movements a baby already uses and adjusting the space and help around them. This is proposed wording, not an approved replacement. Preserve the book’s individual-pace and help qualifications in public detail; do not append outside positioning or material advice.

issues.finding: The instruction about not putting a baby into positions they cannot yet reach themselves broadens a qualified discussion into an absolute rule. It can imply that ordinary lying on the tummy/back or being held must also wait for independent entry into those positions, and can make the depicted tummy position read as an achievement requirement. The original page specifically discusses propping into sitting/standing and separately describes lying on the back or stomach when not held.
issues.suggestedRevision: In descriptive prose, preserve the distinction rather than the broad prohibition: The authors distinguish lying on the back or tummy from propping a baby into sitting or standing before they can get there independently. Retain context that help is available; do not convert this suggested summary back into a positioning command. The source reviewer must review the exact revised wording and reference.

opening.assessment: The observation question, nearby adult, and focus on current movement are respectful. However, the imperative floor-space invitation, Reach label, active tummy scene and Try this together CTA collectively read as movement guidance issued by the companion.
